hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=x^3-2x^2-2x$ and $g(x)=2$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and the solution of $f(x)=g(x)$ can be found by looking for their intersection points.

options.alt: A cubic function graph and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph moves from negative infinity and increases from left to right to point (negative one half, one half), then decreases to around (two, negative four). It increases to the point (three, three) and continues to positive infinity. The horizontal line is at y equals two and intersects the cubic function graph at one point.

hints.content:
The graphs intersect where the $x$-coordinate is approximately $3$.

[[☃ image 1]]

hints.content:
In conclusion, an approximate solution to the equation is $x\approx 3$.

[[☃ explanation 1]]

options.explanation: A cubic graph changes between increasing and decreasing at no more than 2 points. Since we see both those points in the graph, we know the values of the function to the left of the point will all be less than $y=2$ and the values to the right of the point will all be greater than $y=2$. So there are no more intersection points.
options.showPrompt: How do we know that there aren't any other solutions?
